source.title: Films that Build the Prepared Civilian Mindset Vol. 1

closing.q: If the government banned books tomorrow, which three would you risk hiding, and why?
closing.note: Asked at the end of the video.

meta.chaptersNote: The video description lists The Big Country at 39:31; from its position between Apocalypse Now (48:21) and Children of Men (50:40) the correct time is 49:31.

films.title: The Patriot
films.synopsis: A South Carolina planter who meant to sit out the Revolutionary War is pulled in when British regulars reach his family and his land.

questions.q: When is it right to pick up a rifle for a cause? And when is it just ego or revenge dressed up as patriotism?
Which characters actually fight for principles, and who is just following orders or their own emotions?
If something similar happened today, what would guerrilla resistance look like in the town that you live in?

films.title: Snowpiercer
films.synopsis: After a climate experiment freezes the earth, what is left of humanity lives on a train whose cars are a class system with no honest exit.

questions.q: What are the cars on our train (school, media, jobs, politics), and where would you be placed?
Do you think our society allows for real change, or just controlled revolutions that keep the system intact?
What does getting off the train look like in real life for you? Whether it's financial, geographic, maybe your lifestyle, what does it look like?

films.title: District 9
films.synopsis: A Johannesburg bureaucrat sent to evict stranded aliens is contaminated and starts becoming the people the state taught him to move.

questions.q: If you woke up as a prawn tomorrow, what would change about the ways that you see police, corporations, and your neighbors?
How do governments make it socially acceptable to mistreat certain groups?
Have you ever believed a story about a group of people and then later realized it was propaganda or incomplete?

films.title: The Eternaut
films.synopsis: A deadly snowfall drives Buenos Aires indoors. A small circle has to learn what fell, who is lying about it, and how to keep their people alive.

questions.q: Who do you trust more to survive, institutions or your little group of neighbors? And why?

How quickly would you obey an order to stay inside, evacuate, or comply if the sky turned deadly here? How did you act when the COVID lockdowns hit, and regardless of your answer, what did you learn and how would you do it differently next time?
If this happened in your neighborhood, who would you immediately team up with, and who would you immediately start to avoid?

films.title: Andor
films.synopsis: A thief who only wanted to stay alive is hired, compromised, and finally committed to a rebellion that already has accountants and martyrs.

questions.q: What finally pushes Cassian from just trying to survive to “I have to be a part of this fight”?
Which type of characters keep the Empire running more: the true believers, the careerists, or the scared?
If you lived in that universe, what kind of resistance work would fit your personality and your current skill set?

films.title: Chernobyl
films.synopsis: The 1986 reactor explosion, and the officials who treated the truth as a bigger threat than the radiation.

questions.q: Why do so many people go along with obvious lies about the danger?
Do you think our institutions would behave differently in a similar disaster?
What information would you want before an event like this to protect your family?

films.title: The Death of Stalin
films.synopsis: In the hours after Stalin dies, the men who feared him start lying, bargaining, and arranging each other's funerals.

questions.q: Why does everyone in that system lie, even when the truth is obvious?
What parts of modern politics feel like this, where everyone is afraid to say the obvious thing?
Would you rather be safe and silent in that world, or be honest and risk your livelihood, or potentially even your life?

films.title: Johnny Tremain
films.synopsis: A proud Boston apprentice loses the use of his hand and, with his trade, the excuse to stay out of the fight.

questions.q: What changes Johnny from caring only about himself to caring about a larger cause?
How do small personal injustices wake people up politically?
What skill would you want to bring to a movement like the Sons of Liberty?

films.title: Captain Fantastic
films.synopsis: A father who raised his children in the woods is forced to bring them into the society he spent years refusing.

questions.q: Which parts of their lifestyle make the kids strong, free thinkers, and which parts feel like the dad just trying to exert control?
How do you balance protecting your kids from a broken culture versus preparing them to live in it?
What real-world skills from that family do you most want in your own home?

films.title: Braveheart
films.synopsis: William Wallace turns a private killing into a war for Scottish independence, and the film does not pretend the cost stays private.

questions.q: What is one truth that you would be willing to stake your entire life on?
If it cost you everything, is freedom actually worth it?
Where would you draw the line in the sand if the government tried to take something from you forcefully? Where would you actually stand and fight?

films.title: The Matrix
films.synopsis: A programmer learns that his ordinary life is a constructed prison. Getting out is not the same as being ready for what is outside.

questions.q: If the red pill is just uncomfortable truth, what is a red pill that you have taken in your own life?
What modern systems feel the most like the Matrix: news, social media, politics, or is it something else?
If you woke up outside of the Matrix tomorrow, what skill set would you wish you had prepared?
If you could plug into the Matrix and get any skill set in the world, what would it be?

films.title: Swiss Family Robinson
films.synopsis: A shipwrecked family turns a deserted island into a house, a division of labor, and a defense.

trailer.title: Swiss Family Robinson 1960 Trailer | John Mills | Dorothy McGuire

questions.q: Who in your family would fill which role on that island? Are you the builder, the scout, the medic, or the planner?
What do they do right in turning disaster into a home? And what do you think you would do differently?
What is one small island skill or disaster skill that we could realistically practice this year?

films.title: Letters from Iwo Jima
films.synopsis: The battle of Iwo Jima from the Japanese defenders: letters home, a commander who knows the math, and orders that will not be survived.

questions.q: Did this movie change how you see the enemy in a war movie? And how so?
How does propaganda shape the soldiers' expectations versus what actually happens in their position?
Would you obey every order, or would you look for ways to bend or break them?
Throughout American history, if you look at all the wars we've fought, which wars have involved a people (not a nation, but a people) that were actually opposed to …?
questions.note: The end of this bonus question runs into the next segment in the video and is not fully audible; shown as captioned.

films.title: Saints and Soldiers
films.synopsis: After the Malmédy massacre, a few American soldiers try to stay a unit, stay moving, and stay human in the snow.

questions.q: What keeps these guys' morale up in the middle of all of this chaos?
How do faith and doubt show up differently under fire?
What do you think you'd cling to mentally or spiritually in a situation like that?
What about Deacon's character and his actions truly changed the lives of his teammates?

films.title: We Were Soldiers
films.synopsis: Ia Drang, told as a commander who stays on the ground with his men and as the families at home waiting on the casualty list.

questions.q: What does good leadership look like in this film? And who fails to show up as a leader?
How honestly do you think this shows the cost of war on families back at home?
If you were in that unit, what role would you hope to fill?

films.title: Black Hawk Down
films.synopsis: Mogadishu, 1993. A raid breaks into a night of small decisions, casualties, and people who will not leave their own behind.

questions.q: What do you think the soldiers understood about why they were there?
Was there ever a moment when you thought this mission should never have happened? If so, when was that in the film?
What skills, outside of just shooting, seemed most important in all of that chaos?

films.title: Gattaca
films.synopsis: In a society that reads DNA as destiny, a man born with the “wrong” genome borrows another man's identity to reach the stars.

questions.q: If your future were predicted by your DNA at birth, how would your life look different?
Where do we already sort people today based on metrics: scores, tests, and credit?
What are ways to resist being defined by labels that someone else puts on you?
Just for the adults: at what age did you stop giving a crap about what people thought about you?

films.title: Minority Report
films.synopsis: Police arrest people for murders that have not happened yet — until the machine names one of the men who runs it.

questions.q: Is it ever okay to punish people for something that they haven't done yet?
How much freedom would you personally trade in order to guarantee lower crime?
Do you see any pre-crime logic in today's policing, school disputes, or online moderation?

films.title: Silo
films.synopsis: An underground city of 144 levels is told the surface will kill them. A few residents start checking the story.

questions.q: If you grew up in the silo, what details would start making you suspicious of the top level?
Why do you think so many people accepted the rules without ever questioning the outside?
Do you see a form of silo in current society, where people are told to believe whatever the narrative is, and if they start to question it, they get pushed out?

films.title: V for Vendetta
films.synopsis: In a frightened Britain, a masked man and a woman who has already lost too much decide that compliance has gone far enough.

trailer.title: V For Vendetta (2005) Official Trailer #1 - Sc-Fi Thriller HD

questions.q: Do you ever feel like division is sown in order to keep people from uniting?
Do heroes always do what is right, or can they get it wrong at times?
What freedoms did people in that world give up first, and why?
At what point would you decide, “Okay, now I have to resist,” even if it's dangerous?
Do you think symbols like the mask are powerful or cringe? Do they help or hurt a movement, and why?

films.title: Soylent Green
films.synopsis: New York is overcrowded, food is a ration, and the ration has a source the public is not supposed to name.

questions.q: Does this story make you rethink the FDA food pyramid and how nutrition is pushed on general society?
How dependent are we right now on systems that we never question, especially around food?
Do you think governments and those in political power are actually the ones pulling the strings, or do they have a master as well?

films.title: The Road
films.synopsis: A father and son walk a burned country with a cart, a pistol, and a rule they keep repeating: we are the good guys.

questions.q: In that world, what does it mean to be one of the good guys? What does it look like?
Would you rather stay moving like the father and son, or try to build up a fort or a small community?
What is one item or skill you saw that you think would matter most in a situation like that?

films.title: The Searchers
films.synopsis: A Confederate veteran spends years hunting the people who took his niece. The longer he hunts, the clearer it is what the hunt has made him.

questions.q: Is the role that John Wayne plays actually a good person? And what does it mean to be a good person?
Is what John Wayne did when he found Debbie the right course of action, or should he have done something different?
The way John Wayne treats other characters around him in the story is pretty rough. Why do you think that is?

films.title: The Life of David Gale
films.synopsis: A death-penalty opponent sits on death row while a reporter tries to tell whether the case is justice or a staged argument.

trailer.title: The Life of David Gale Official Trailer #1 - Kevin Spacey Movie (2003) HD

questions.q: Which crimes should actually be punishable by death?
What flaws in our current justice system would have to be corrected to guarantee that no innocent person was put to death by the state?
Which would be worse: a hundred guilty men being set free, or one innocent man being put to death?

films.title: Apocalypse Now
films.synopsis: A captain is sent upriver to kill a colonel who stopped taking orders. The official mission and the war he finds are not the same thing.

trailer.title: APOCALYPSE NOW - Official Trailer - Back in Cinemas for Limited Time!

questions.q: At what point do you think the main character starts to lose his own moral compass? Or does he even?
How does the film show the difference between the official mission and what war actually turns into?
Do you think you could stay sane in an environment like that? Why or why not?

films.title: The Big Country
films.synopsis: A newcomer who will not duel on command walks into a land feud where both families treat refusal as cowardice.

questions.q: How do you see peer pressure working on the main character throughout the film?
What does real courage look like here? Is it fighting, or is it refusing to fight, or maybe something else?
Where in this story do you figure out that the main family is the bad family?

films.title: Children of Men
films.synopsis: In a Britain that can no longer have children, one pregnant woman becomes the only concrete argument that there is a future.

trailer.title: Children of Men Official Trailer #1 - Julianne Moore, Clive Owen Movie (2006) HD

questions.q: How do people act differently in a world where there's no chance of a future generation?
What parts of that society feel uncomfortably close to the one that we're currently living in?

Would you risk your life for the baby in that story? What would be going through your mind? And would you still risk your life if you had your own family to take care of, and you weren't just a solo guy like Clive Owen was?

films.title: Rescue Dawn
films.synopsis: A shot-down pilot plans an escape from a jungle prison while the men in the cell come apart in different ways.

questions.q: How do you hold on to hope when every rational sign says you are not getting out?
What different ways do the POWs cope mentally? And which character do you relate to the most?
If you're planning an escape, which friend or family member of yours would you want to be in the cell with you, or not want to be in the cell with you?

films.title: The Impossible
films.synopsis: A vacationing family is torn apart by the 2004 tsunami and put back together mostly by strangers, not by institutions.

questions.q: What choices did the family make before the tsunami that either helped or hurt them during it?
How did normal people, not institutions, become the main source of rescue and care?
Does this make you want to do anything different about how you vacation or travel?

films.title: A Quiet Place
films.synopsis: Creatures hunt by sound, so a family's habits, chores, and children are now a single tactical problem.

questions.q: How would your habits have to change tomorrow if suddenly sound meant death?
What do you think they did best as a family in terms of planning and communication?
What are the responsibilities that each person in this family has in order to protect the family as a whole?

films.title: Jericho
films.synopsis: After nuclear strikes on American cities, a Kansas town has to decide who is in charge, what the radios are hiding, and how long “temporary” lasts.

questions.q: In the first few episodes, what small details tell you that this isn't just a temporary crisis?
Who becomes more valuable in the town after the crisis, who loses influence, and why?
What role does the main character actually play in all of this? He doesn't have one specific job, so what roles does he have to fill?
